reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is distinguishing text (low contrast, arbitrary shape) from cluttered backgrounds (fabric, occlusions). The authors exploit two complementary cues: (1) edges and boundaries (captured by gradient magnitude) and (2) spatial coherence of skin-like textures (via directional coherence and clustering). This dual-filtering approach creates a saliency map highlighting potential text locations. Mathematically, it is a weighted sum of two non-negative tensors, ensuring positivity and interpretability. However, the method assumes that text always forms sharp edges; curved or thin fonts may blur these gradients, leading to missed detections. Additionally, the reliance on K-means clustering makes the algorithm sensitive to initialization and prone to over-segmentation when multiple object classes coexist in the same image.
